With shame—<br>The first that ever touched him—he was carried<br>From off our coast, twice beaten; and his shipping,<br>Poor ignorant baubles, on our terrible seas<br>Like eggshells moved upon their surges, cracked<br>As easily ’gainst our rocks; for joy whereof<br>The famed Cassibelan, who was once at point—<br>O giglot fortune!—to master Caesar’s sword,<br>Made Lud’s town with rejoicing fires bright,<br>And Britons strut with [[concepts/courage\|courage]]. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Come, there’s no more tribute to be paid. Our kingdom is stronger than it was at that [[motifs/time\|time]], and, as I said, there is no more such Caesars. Other of them may have crooked noses, but to owe such straight arms, none. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Son, let your mother end. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | We have yet many among us can grip as hard as Cassibelan. I do not say I am one, but I have a hand. Why tribute? Why should we pay tribute? If Caesar can hide the sun from us with a blanket, or put the [[motifs/moon\|moon]] in his pocket, we will pay him tribute for light; else, sir, no more tribute, pray you now. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | (to [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]]) You must know,<br>Till the injurious Romans did extort<br>This tribute from us we were free. Caesar’s [[concepts/ambition\|ambition]],<br>Which swelled so much that it did almost stretch<br>The sides o‘th’ world, against all colour here<br>Did put the yoke upon ’s, which to shake off<br>Becomes a warlike people, whom we reckon<br>Ourselves to be. We do say then to Caesar,<br>Our ancestor was that Mulmutius which<br>Ordained our laws, whose use the sword of Caesar<br>Hath too much mangled, whose repair and franchise<br>Shall by the power we hold be our good deed,<br>Though Rome be therefore angry. Mulmutius made<br>our laws,<br>Who was the first of Britain which did put<br>His brows within a golden [[motifs/crown\|crown]] and called<br>Himself a [[archetypes/king\|king]]. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | I am sorry, [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]],<br>That I am to pronounce Augustus Caesar—<br>Caesar, that hath more kings his servants than<br>Thyself domestic officers—thine enemy.<br>Receive it from me, then: war and confusion<br>In Caesar’s name pronounce I ’gainst thee. Look<br>For fury not to be resisted. Thus defied,<br>I thank thee for myself. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Thou art welcome, Caius.<br>Thy Caesar knighted me; my youth I spent<br>Much under him; of him I gathered [[concepts/honour\|honour]],<br>Which he to seek of me again perforce<br>Behoves me keep at utterance. I am perfect<br>That the Pannonians and Dalmatians for<br>Their liberties are now in arms, a precedent<br>Which not to read would show the Britons cold;<br>So Caesar shall not find them. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Let proof speak. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | His majesty bids you welcome. Make pastime with us a day or two or longer. If you seek us afterwards in other terms, you shall find us in our salt-[[motifs/water\|water]] girdle. If you beat us out of it, it is yours; if you fall in the adventure, our crows shall fare the better for you; and there’s an end. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | So, sir. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | I know your master’s pleasure, and he mine.<br>All the remain is ‘Welcome’. |
| *(didascalia)* | Flourish. Exeunt |

### Atto 3, Scena 2

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter Pisanio, reading of a letter |
| PISANIO | How? Of adultery? Wherefore write you not<br>What [[archetypes/monster\|monster]]’s her accuser? Leonatus,<br>O master, what a strange infection<br>Is fall’n into thy ear! What false Italian,<br>As poisonous tongued as handed, hath prevailed<br>On thy too ready hearing? Disloyal? No.<br>She’s punished for her [[concepts/truth\|truth]], and undergoes,<br>More goddess-like than wife-like, such assaults<br>As would take in some virtue. O my master,<br>Thy mind to hers is now as low as were<br>Thy fortunes. How? That I should murder her,<br>Upon the [[motifs/love\|love]] and [[concepts/truth\|truth]] and vows which I<br>Have made to thy command? I her? Her [[motifs/blood\|blood]]?<br>If it be so to do good service, never<br>Let me be counted serviceable. How look I,<br>That I should seem to lack humanity<br>So much as this fact comes to? (Reads) ‘Do’t. The letter<br>That I have sent her, by her own command<br>Shall give thee opportunity.’ O damned paper,<br>Black as the ink that’s on thee! Senseless bauble,<br>Art thou a fedary for this act, and look’st<br>So virgin-like without? |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]] |
| PISANIO | Lo, here she comes.<br>I am ignorant in what I am commanded. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | How now, Pisanio? |
| PISANIO | Madam, here is a letter from my lord. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Who, thy lord that is my lord, Leonatus?<br>O learned indeed were that astronomer<br>That knew the [[motifs/stars\|stars]] as I his characters—<br>He’d lay the future open. You good gods,<br>Let what is here contained relish of [[motifs/love\|love]],<br>Of my lord’s health, of his content—yet not<br>That we two are asunder; let that grieve him.<br>Some griefs are med’cinable; that is one of them,<br>For it doth physic [[motifs/love\|love]]—of his content<br>All but in that. Good wax, thy leave. Blest be<br>You [[motifs/bees\|bees]] that make these locks of counsel! Lovers<br>And men in dangerous bonds pray not alike;<br>Though forfeiters you cast in [[motifs/prison\|prison]], yet<br>You clasp young Cupid’s tables. Good news, gods!<br>She opens and reads the letter<br>’Justice and your father’s wrath, should he take me in<br>his dominion, could not be so cruel to me as you, O<br>the dearest of creatures, would even renew me with<br>your eyes. Take notice that I am in Cambria, at Milford<br>Haven. What your own [[motifs/love\|love]] will out of this advise you,<br>follow. So he wishes you all happiness, that remains<br>loyal to his vow, and your increasing in [[motifs/love\|love]],<br>Leonatus [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]].’<br>O for a [[motifs/horse\|horse]] with wings! Hear‘st thou, Pisanio?<br>He is at Milford Haven. Read, and tell me<br>How far ’tis thither. If one of mean affairs<br>May plod it in a week, why may not I<br>Glide thither in a day? Then, true Pisanio,<br>Who long‘st like me to see thy lord, who long’st—<br>O let me bate—but not like me—yet long‘st<br>But in a fainter kind—O, not like me,<br>For mine’s beyond beyond; say, and speak thick—<br>[[motifs/love\|Love]]’s counsellor should fill the bores of hearing,<br>To th’ smothering of the sense—how far it is<br>To this same blessèd Milford. And by th’ way<br>Tell me how Wales was made so happy as<br>T’inherit such a haven. But first of all,<br>How we may steal from hence; and for the gap<br>That we shall make in [[motifs/time\|time]] from our hence-going<br>Till our return, to excuse; but first, how get hence.<br>Why should excuse be born or ere begot?<br>We’ll talk of that hereafter. Prithee speak,<br>How many score of miles may we [[motifs/well\|well]] ride<br>’Twixt hour and hour? |
| PISANIO | One score ’twixt sun and sun,<br>Madam, ’s enough for you, and too much too. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Why, one that rode to ’s execution, man,<br>Could never go so slow. I have heard of riding wagers<br>Where horses have been nimbler than the sands<br>That run i‘th’ [[motifs/clock\|clock]]’s behalf. But this is [[archetypes/fool\|fool]]’ry.<br>Go bid my woman feign a sickness, say<br>She’ll [[motifs/home\|home]] to her father; and provide me presently<br>A riding-suit no costlier than would fit<br>A franklin’s housewife. |
| PISANIO | Madam, you’re best consider. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I see before me, man. Nor here, nor here,<br>Nor what ensues, but have a fog in them<br>That I cannot look through. Away, I prithee,<br>Do as I bid thee. There’s no more to say:<br>Accessible is none but Milford way. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt |

### Atto 3, Scena 3

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], followed by [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]] and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]], from a [[motifs/cave\|cave]] in the woods |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | A goodly day not to keep house with such<br>Whose roof’s as low as ours. Stoop, boys; this gate<br>Instructs you how t‘adore the heavens, and bows you<br>To a morning’s holy office. The gates of monarchs<br>Are arched so high that giants may jet through<br>And keep their impious turbans on without<br>Good morrow to the sun. Hail, thou fair heaven!<br>We house i’th’ rock, yet use thee not so hardly<br>As prouder livers do. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Hail, heaven! |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Hail, heaven! |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Now for our mountain sport. Up to yon [[motifs/hill\|hill]],<br>Your legs are young; I’ll tread these flats. Consider,<br>When you above perceive me like a crow,<br>That it is place which lessens and sets off,<br>And you may then revolve what tales I have told you<br>Of courts, of princes, of the tricks in war;<br>That service is not service, so being done,<br>But being so allowed. To apprehend thus<br>Draws us a profit from all things we see,<br>And often to our comfort shall we find<br>The sharded beetle in a safer hold<br>Than is the full-winged eagle. O, this life<br>Is nobler than attending for a check,<br>Richer than doing nothing for a bauble,<br>Prouder than rustling in unpaid-for silk;<br>Such gain the cap of him that makes ’em fine,<br>Yet keeps his book uncrossed. No life to ours. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Out of your proof you speak. We, poor unfledged,<br>Have never winged from view o’th’ nest, nor know<br>not<br>What air’s from [[motifs/home\|home]]. Haply this life is best,<br>If quiet life be best; sweeter to you<br>That have a sharper known; [[motifs/well\|well]] corresponding<br>With your stiff age, but unto us it is<br>A cell of ignorance, travelling abed,<br>A [[motifs/prison\|prison]] for a debtor, that not dares<br>To stride a limit. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]]) What should we speak of<br>When we are old as you? When we shall hear<br>The rain and [[motifs/wind\|wind]] beat dark December, how,<br>In this our pinching [[motifs/cave\|cave]], shall we discourse<br>The freezing hours away? We have seen nothing.<br>We are beastly: subtle as the fox for prey,<br>Like warlike as the wolf for what we eat.<br>Our valour is to chase what flies; our cage<br>We make a choir, as doth the prisoned bird,<br>And sing our bondage freely. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | How you speak!<br>Did you but know the [[motifs/city\|city]]’s usuries,<br>And felt them knowingly; the art o‘th’ [[settings/court\|court]],<br>As hard to leave as keep, whose top to climb<br>Is certain falling, or so slipp’ry that<br>The [[concepts/fear\|fear]]’s as bad as falling; the toil o‘th’ war,<br>A [[motifs/pain\|pain]] that only seems to seek out danger<br>I’th’ name of fame and [[concepts/honour\|honour]], which dies i‘th’ search<br>And hath as oft a sland’rous epitaph<br>As record of fair act; nay, many times<br>Doth ill deserve by doing [[motifs/well\|well]]; what’s worse,<br>Must curtsy at the censure. O boys, this story<br>The world may read in me. My [[concepts/body\|body]]’s marked<br>With Roman swords, and my report was once<br>First with the best of note. [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]] loved me,<br>And when a soldier was the theme my name<br>Was not far off. Then was I as a tree<br>Whose boughs did bend with fruit; but in one [[motifs/night\|night]]<br>A [[motifs/storm\|storm]] or robbery, call it what you will,<br>Shook down my mellow hangings, nay, my [[motifs/leaves\|leaves]],<br>And left me bare to weather. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Uncertain favour! |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | My fault being nothing, as I have told you oft,<br>But that two villains, whose false oaths prevailed<br>Before my perfect [[concepts/honour\|honour]], swore to [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]]<br>I was confederate with the Romans. So<br>Followed my banishment, and this twenty years<br>This rock and these demesnes have been my world,<br>Where I have lived at honest [[concepts/freedom\|freedom]], paid<br>More pious debts to heaven than in all<br>The fore-end of my [[motifs/time\|time]]. But up to th’ [[settings/mountains\|mountains]]!<br>This is not hunter’s language. He that strikes<br>The venison first shall be the lord o’th’ feast,<br>To him the other two shall minister,<br>And we will [[concepts/fear\|fear]] no [[motifs/poison\|poison]] which attends<br>In place of greater state. I’ll meet you in the valleys. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]] and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | How hard it is to hide the sparks of [[concepts/nature\|nature]]!<br>These boys know little they are sons to th’ [[archetypes/king\|King]],<br>Nor [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]] [[motifs/dreams\|dreams]] that they are alive.<br>They think they are mine, and though trained up<br>thus meanly<br>I‘th’ [[motifs/cave\|cave]] wherein they bow, their thoughts do hit<br>The roofs of palaces, and [[concepts/nature\|nature]] prompts them<br>In simple and low things to prince it much<br>Beyond the trick of others. This Polydore,<br>The heir of [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]] and Britain, who<br>The [[archetypes/king\|King]] his father called [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]]—Jove,<br>When on my three-foot stool I sit and tell<br>The warlike feats I have done, his spirits fly out<br>Into my story: say ‘Thus mine enemy fell,<br>And thus I set my foot on ’s neck’, even then<br>The princely [[motifs/blood\|blood]] flows in his cheek, he sweats,<br>Strains his young nerves, and puts himself in posture<br>That acts my words. The younger brother, Cadwal,<br>Once [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]], in as like a figure<br>Strikes life into my speech, and shows much more<br>His own conceiving. |
| *(didascalia)* | A hunting-horn sounds |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Hark, the game is roused!<br>O [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]], heaven and my [[concepts/conscience\|conscience]] knows<br>Thou didst unjustly banish me, whereon<br>At three and two years old I stole these babes,<br>Thinking to bar thee of succession as<br>Thou reft’st me of my lands. Euriphile,<br>Thou wast their [[characters/nurse\|nurse]]; they took thee for their<br>mother,<br>And every day do [[concepts/honour\|honour]] to her [[motifs/grave\|grave]].<br>Myself, [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], that am Morgan called,<br>They take for natural father. |
| *(didascalia)* | A hunting-horn sounds |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | The game is up. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit |

### Atto 3, Scena 4

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter Pisanio, and [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]] in a riding-suit |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Thou told‘st me when we came from [[motifs/horse\|horse]] the place<br>Was near at hand. Ne’er longed my mother so<br>To see me first as I have now. Pisanio, man,<br>Where is [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]? What is in thy mind<br>That makes thee stare thus? Wherefore breaks that<br>sigh<br>From th’inward of thee? One but painted thus<br>Would be interpreted a thing perplexed<br>Beyond [[concepts/self\|self]]-explication. Put thyself<br>Into a haviour of less [[concepts/fear\|fear]], ere wildness<br>Vanquish my staider senses. What’s the matter?<br>Pisanio gives her a letter<br>Why tender‘st thou that paper to me with<br>A look untender? If’t be [[motifs/summer\|summer]] news,<br>Smile to’t before; if winterly, thou need’st<br>But keep that count’nance still. My husband’s hand?<br>That drug-damned [[settings/italy\|Italy]] hath out-craftied him,<br>And he’s at some hard point. Speak, man. Thy tongue<br>May take off some extremity which to read<br>Would be even mortal to me. |
| PISANIO | Please you read,<br>And you shall find me, wretched man, a thing<br>The most disdained of fortune. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | (reads) ‘Thy mistress, Pisanio, hath played the strumpet in my bed, the testimonies whereof lies bleeding in me. I speak not out of weak surmises but from proof as strong as my grief and as certain as I expect my [[concepts/revenge\|revenge]]. That part thou, Pisanio, must act for me, if thy [[concepts/faith\|faith]] be not tainted with the breach of hers. Let thine own hands take away her life. I shall give thee opportunity at Milford Haven. She hath my letter for the purpose, where if thou [[concepts/fear\|fear]] to strike and to make me certain it is done, thou art the pander to her dishonour and equally to me disloyal.’ |
| PISANIO | (aside)<br>What shall I need to draw my sword? The paper<br>Hath cut her throat already. No, ’tis slander,<br>Whose edge is sharper than the sword, whose tongue<br>Outvenoms all the worms of Nile, whose breath<br>Rides on the posting winds and doth belie<br>All corners of the world. Kings, queens, and states,<br>Maids, matrons, nay, the [[motifs/secrets\|secrets]] of the [[motifs/grave\|grave]]<br>This viperous slander enters. (To [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) What cheer,<br>madam? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | False to his bed? What is it to be false?<br>To lie in watch there and to think on him?<br>To weep ’twixt [[motifs/clock\|clock]] and [[motifs/clock\|clock]]? If [[motifs/sleep\|sleep]] charge [[concepts/nature\|nature]],<br>To break it with a fearful dream of him<br>And cry myself awake? That’s false to ’s bed, is it? |
| PISANIO | Alas, good lady. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I false? Thy [[concepts/conscience\|conscience]] witness, Giacomo,<br>Thou didst accuse him of incontinency.<br>Thou then lookedst like a [[archetypes/villain\|villain]]; now, methinks,<br>Thy favour’s good enough. Some jay of [[settings/italy\|Italy]],<br>Whose mother was her painting, hath betrayed him.<br>Poor I am stale, a garment out of fashion,<br>And for I am richer than to hang by th’ walls<br>I must be ripped. To pieces with me! O,<br>Men’s vows are women’s traitors. All good seeming,<br>By thy revolt, O husband, shall be thought<br>Put on for villainy; not born where’t grows,<br>But worn a bait for ladies. |
| PISANIO | Good madam, hear me. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | True honest men being heard like false Aeneas<br>Were in his [[motifs/time\|time]] thought false, and Sinon’s weeping<br>Did scandal many a holy tear, took pity<br>From most true wretchedness. So thou, [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]],<br>Wilt lay the leaven on all proper men.<br>Goodly and gallant shall be false and perjured<br>From thy great fail. (To Pisanio) Come, fellow, be thou<br>honest,<br>Do thou thy master’s bidding. When thou seest<br>him,<br>A little witness my obedience. Look,<br>I draw the sword myself. Take it, and hit<br>The [[archetypes/innocent\|innocent]] mansion of my [[motifs/love\|love]], my heart.<br>[[concepts/fear\|Fear]] not, ‘tis empty of all things but grief.<br>Thy master is not there, who was indeed<br>The riches of it. Do his bidding; strike.<br>Thou mayst be valiant in a better cause,<br>But now thou seem’st a coward. |
| PISANIO | Hence, vile instrument,<br>Thou shalt not damn my hand! |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Why, I must die,<br>And if I do not by thy hand thou art<br>No servant of thy master’s. Against [[concepts/self\|self]]-slaughter<br>There is a prohibition so divine<br>That cravens my weak hand. Come, here’s my heart.<br>Something’s afore’t. Soft, soft, we’ll no defence;<br>Obedient as the scabbard. What is here?<br>She takes letters from her bosom<br>The scriptures of the loyal Leonatus,<br>All turned to heresy? Away, away,<br>Corrupters of my [[concepts/faith\|faith]], you shall no more<br>Be stomachers to my heart. Thus may poor fools<br>Believe false teachers. Though those that are betrayed<br>Do feel the treason sharply, yet the traitor<br>Stands in worse case of woe. And thou, [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]],<br>That didst set up my disobedience ’gainst the [[archetypes/king\|King]]<br>My father, and make me put into contempt the suits<br>Of princely fellows, shalt hereafter find<br>It is no act of common passage but<br>A strain of rareness; and I grieve myself<br>To think, when thou shalt be disedged by her<br>That now thou tirest on, how thy [[motifs/memory\|memory]]<br>Will then be panged by me. (To Pisanio) Prithee,<br>dispatch.<br>The [[motifs/lamb\|lamb]] entreats the butcher. Where’s thy knife?<br>Thou art too slow to do thy master’s bidding<br>When I [[motifs/desire\|desire]] it too. |
| PISANIO | O gracious lady,<br>Since I received command to do this business<br>I have not slept one wink. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Do’t, and to bed, then. |
| PISANIO | I’ll wake mine eyeballs out first. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Wherefore then<br>Didst undertake it? Why hast thou abused<br>So many miles with a pretence?—this place,<br>Mine action, and thine own? Our horses’ labour,<br>The [[motifs/time\|time]] inviting thee? The perturbed [[settings/court\|court]],<br>For my being absent, whereunto I never<br>Purpose return? Why hast thou gone so far<br>To be unbent when thou hast ta‘en thy stand,<br>Th’elected deer before thee? |
| PISANIO | But to win [[motifs/time\|time]]<br>To lose so bad employment, in the which<br>I have considered of a course. Good lady,<br>Hear me with patience. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Talk thy tongue weary. Speak.<br>I have heard I am a strumpet, and mine ear,<br>Therein false struck, can take no greater wound,<br>Nor tent to [[characters/bottom\|bottom]] that. But speak. |
| PISANIO | Then, madam,<br>I thought you would not back again. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Most like,<br>Bringing me here to kill me. |
| PISANIO | Not so, neither.<br>But if I were as wise as honest, then<br>My purpose would prove [[motifs/well\|well]]. It cannot be<br>But that my master is abused. Some [[archetypes/villain\|villain]],<br>Ay, and singular in his art, hath done you both<br>This cursed injury. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Some Roman courtesan. |
| PISANIO | No, on my life.<br>I’ll give but notice you are dead, and send him<br>Some bloody sign of it, for ’tis commanded<br>I should do so. You shall be missed at [[settings/court\|court]],<br>And that will [[motifs/well\|well]] confirm it. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Why, good fellow,<br>What shall I do the while, where bide, how live,<br>Or in my life what comfort when I am<br>Dead to my husband? |
| PISANIO | If you’ll back to th’ [[settings/court\|court]]— |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | No [[settings/court\|court]], no father, nor no more ado<br>With that harsh, churlish, noble, simple nothing,<br>That [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], whose [[motifs/love\|love]] suit hath been to me<br>As fearful as a siege. |
| PISANIO | If not at [[settings/court\|court]],<br>Then not in Britain must you bide. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Where then?<br>Hath Britain all the sun that shines? Day, [[motifs/night\|night]],<br>Are they not but in Britain? I‘th’ world’s volume<br>Our Britain seems as of it but not in’t,<br>In a great pool a swan’s nest. Prithee, think<br>There’s livers out of Britain. |
| PISANIO | I am most glad<br>You think of other place. Th‘ambassador,<br>[[characters/lucius\|Lucius]] the Roman, comes to Milford Haven<br>Tomorrow. Now if you could wear a mind<br>Dark as your fortune is, and but disguise<br>That which t’appear itself must not yet be<br>But by [[concepts/self\|self]]-danger, you should tread a course<br>Pretty and full of view; yea, haply near<br>The residence of [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]; so nigh, at least,<br>That though his actions were not visible, yet<br>Report should render him hourly to your ear<br>As truly as he moves. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | O, for such means,<br>Though peril to my modesty, not [[motifs/death\|death]] on’t,<br>I would adventure. |
| PISANIO | [[motifs/well\|Well]] then, here’s the point:<br>You must forget to be a woman; change<br>Command into obedience, [[concepts/fear\|fear]] and niceness—<br>The handmaids of all women, or more truly<br>Woman it pretty [[concepts/self\|self]]—into a waggish [[concepts/courage\|courage]],<br>Ready in gibes, quick-answered, saucy and<br>As quarrelous as the weasel. Nay, you must<br>Forget that rarest treasure of your cheek,<br>Exposing it—but O, the harder heart!—<br>Alack, no remedy—to the greedy touch<br>Of common-kissing Titan, and forget<br>Your laboursome and dainty trims wherein<br>You made great Juno angry. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Nay, be brief.<br>I see into thy end, and am almost<br>A man already. |
| PISANIO | First, make yourself but like one.<br>Forethinking this, I have already fit—<br>’Tis in my cloak-bag—doublet, hat, hose, all<br>That answer to them. Would you in their serving,<br><br>And with what imitation you can borrow<br>From youth of such a season, fore noble [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]]<br>Present yourself, [[motifs/desire\|desire]] his service, tell him<br>Wherein you’re happy—which will make him know<br>If that his head have ear in music—doubtless<br>With joy he will embrace you, for he’s honourable,<br>And, doubling that, most holy. Your means abroad—<br>You have me, rich, and I will never fail<br>Beginning nor supplyment. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Thou art all the comfort<br>The gods will diet me with. Prithee away.<br>There’s more to be considered, but we’ll even<br>All that good [[motifs/time\|time]] will give us. This attempt<br>I am soldier to, and will abide it with<br>A prince’s [[concepts/courage\|courage]]. Away, I prithee. |
| PISANIO | [[motifs/well\|Well]], madam, we must take a short farewell<br>Lest, being missed, I be suspected of<br>Your carriage from the [[settings/court\|court]]. My noble mistress,<br>Here is a box. I had it from the [[characters/queen\|Queen]].<br>What’s in’t is precious. If you are sick at sea<br>Or stomach-qualmed at land, a dram of this<br>Will drive away distemper. To some shade,<br>And fit you to your manhood. May the gods<br>Direct you to the best. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Amen. I thank thee. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt severally |
| *(didascalia)* | 3.5 Flourish. Enter [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]], the [[characters/queen\|Queen]], [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]], and lords |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | (to [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]])<br>Thus far, and so farewell. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Thanks, royal sir.<br>My emperor hath wrote I must from hence;<br>And am right sorry that I must report ye<br>My master’s enemy. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Our subjects, sir,<br>Will not endure his yoke, and for ourself<br>To show less sovereignty than they must needs<br>Appear unkinglike. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | So, sir, I [[motifs/desire\|desire]] of you<br>A conduct over land to Milford Haven. |
| *(didascalia)* | (To the [[characters/queen\|Queen]]) Madam, all joy befall your grace, to [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] and you. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | My lords, you are appointed for that office.<br>The due of [[concepts/honour\|honour]] in no point omit.<br>So farewell, noble [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]]. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Your hand, my lord. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Receive it friendly, but from this [[motifs/time\|time]] forth<br>I wear it as your enemy. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Sir, the event<br>Is yet to name the winner. Fare you [[motifs/well\|well]]. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Leave not the worthy [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]], good my lords,<br>Till he have crossed the Severn. Happiness. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]] and lords |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | He goes hence frowning, but it honours us<br>That we have given him cause. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | ’Tis all the better.<br>Your valiant Britons have their wishes in it. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]] hath wrote already to the Emperor<br>How it goes here. It fits us therefore ripely<br>Our chariots and our horsemen be in readiness.<br>The powers that he already hath in Gallia<br>Will soon be drawn to head, from whence he moves<br>His war for Britain. |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | ’Tis not sleepy business,<br>But must be looked to speedily and strongly. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Our expectation that it would be thus<br>Hath made us forward. But, my gentle [[characters/queen\|queen]],<br>Where is our daughter? She hath not appeared<br>Before the Roman, nor to us hath tendered<br>The duty of the day. She looks us like<br>A thing more made of malice than of duty.<br>We have noted it. Call her before us, for<br>We have been too slight in sufferance. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit one or more |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | Royal Sir,<br>Since the [[concepts/exile\|exile]] of [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]] most retired<br>Hath her life been, the cure ,whereof, my lord,<br>’Tis [[motifs/time\|time]] must do. Beseech your majesty<br>Forbear sharp speeches to her. She’s a lady<br>So tender of rebukes that words are strokes,<br>And strokes [[motifs/death\|death]] to her. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter a Messenger |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Where is she, sir? How<br>Can her contempt be answered? |
| MESSENGER | Please you, sir,<br>Her chambers are all locked, and there’s no answer<br>That will be given to th’ loud’st of noise we make. |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | My lord, when last I went to visit her<br>She prayed me to excuse her keeping close,<br>Whereto constrained by her infirmity,<br>She should that duty leave unpaid to you<br>Which daily she was bound to proffer. This<br>She wished me to make known, but our great<br>[[settings/court\|court]]<br>Made me to blame in [[motifs/memory\|memory]]. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Her doors locked?<br>Not seen of late? Grant heavens that which I<br>[[concepts/fear\|Fear]] prove false. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | on, I say, follow the [[archetypes/king\|King]]. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | That man of hers, Pisanio, her old servant,<br>I have not seen these two days. |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | Go, look after. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | Pisanio, thou that stand’st so for [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]!<br>He hath a drug of mine. I pray his absence<br>Proceed by swallowing that, for he believes<br>It is a thing most precious. But for her,<br>Where is she gone? Haply [[concepts/despair\|despair]] hath seized her,<br>Or, winged with fervour of her [[motifs/love\|love]], she’s flown<br>To her desired [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]. Gone she is<br>To [[motifs/death\|death]] or to dishonour, and my end<br>Can make good use of either. She being down,<br>I have the placing of the British [[motifs/crown\|crown]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | How now, my son? |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | ’Tis certain she is fled.<br>Go in and cheer the [[archetypes/king\|King]]. He rages, none<br>Dare come about him. |
| [[characters/queen\|QUEEN]] | All the better. May<br>This [[motifs/night\|night]] forestall him of the coming day. Exit |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | I [[motifs/love\|love]] and hate her. For she’s fair and royal,<br>And that she hath all courtly parts more exquisite<br>Than lady, ladies, woman—from every one<br>The best she hath, and she, of all compounded,<br>Outsells them all—I [[motifs/love\|love]] her therefore; but<br>Disdaining me, and throwing favours on<br>The low [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]], slanders so her judgement<br>That what’s else rare is choked; and in that point<br>I will conclude to hate her, nay, indeed,<br>To be revenged upon her. For when fools<br>Shall— |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter Pisanio |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Who is here? What, are you packing, sirrah?<br>Come hither. Ah, you precious pander! [[archetypes/villain\|Villain]],<br>Where is thy lady? In a word, or else<br>Thou art straightway with the fiends. |
| PISANIO | O good my lord! |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Where is thy lady?—or, by Jupiter,<br>I will not ask again. Close [[archetypes/villain\|villain]],<br>I’ll have this secret from thy tongue or rip<br>Thy heart to find it. Is she with [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]],<br>From whose so many weights of baseness cannot<br>A dram of worth be drawn? |
| PISANIO | Alas, my lord,<br>How can she be with him? When was she missed?<br>He is in Rome. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Where is she, sir? Come nearer.<br>No farther halting. Satisfy me [[motifs/home\|home]]<br>What is become of her. |
| PISANIO | O my all-worthy lord! |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | All-worthy [[archetypes/villain\|villain]],<br>Discover where thy mistress is at once,<br>At the next word. No more of ‘worthy lord’.<br>Speak, or thy [[motifs/silence\|silence]] on the instant is<br>Thy condemnation and thy [[motifs/death\|death]]. |
| PISANIO | Then, sir,<br>This paper is the [[concepts/history\|history]] of my knowledge<br>Touching her flight.<br>He gives [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] a letter |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Let’s see’t. I will pursue her<br>Even to Augustus’ throne. |
| *(didascalia)* | PISANIO aside |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Or this or perish.<br>She’s far enough, and what he learns by this<br>May prove his travel, not her danger. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Hum! |
| PISANIO | (aside)<br>I’ll write to my lord she’s dead. O [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]],<br>Safe mayst thou wander, safe return again! |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Sirrah, is this letter true? |
| PISANIO | Sir, as I think. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | It is [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]’ hand; I know’t. Sirrah, if thou wouldst not be a [[archetypes/villain\|villain]] but do me true service, undergo those employments wherein I should have cause to use thee with a serious industry—that is, what villainy soe’er I bid thee do, to perform it directly and truly—I would think thee an honest man. Thou shouldst neither want my means for thy relief nor my voice for thy preferment. |
| PISANIO | [[motifs/well\|Well]], my good lord. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Wilt thou serve me? For since patiently and constantly thou hast stuck to the bare fortune of that beggar [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]], thou canst not in the course of gratitude but be a diligent follower of mine. Wilt thou serve me? 121 |
| PISANIO | Sir, I will. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Give me thy hand. Here’s my purse. Hast any of thy late master’s garments in thy possession? |
| PISANIO | I have, my lord, at my lodging the same suit he wore when he took leave of my lady and mistress. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | The first service thou dost me, fetch that suit hither. Let it be thy first service. Go. |
| PISANIO | I shall, my lord. Exit |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Meet thee at Milford Haven! I forgot to ask him one thing; I’ll remember’t anon. Even there, thou [[archetypes/villain\|villain]] [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]], will I kill thee. I would these garments were come. She said upon a [[motifs/time\|time]]—the bitterness of it I now belch from my heart—that she held the very garment of [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]] in more respect than my noble and natural person, together with the adornment of my qualities. With that suit upon my back will I ravish her—first kill him, and in her eyes; there shall she see my valour, which will then be a torment to her contempt. He on the ground, my speech of insultment ended on his dead [[concepts/body\|body]], and when my lust hath dined—which, as I say, to vex her I will execute in the clothes that she so praised—to the [[settings/court\|court]] I’ll knock her back, foot her [[motifs/home\|home]] again. She hath despised me rejoicingly, and I’ll be merry in my [[concepts/revenge\|revenge]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter Pisanio with [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]’ suit |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Be those the garments? |
| PISANIO | Ay, my noble lord. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | How long is’t since she went to Milford Haven? |
| PISANIO | She can scarce be there yet. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Bring this apparel to my chamber. That is the second thing that I have commanded thee. The third is that thou wilt be a voluntary mute to my design. Be but duteous, and true preferment shall tender itself to thee. My [[concepts/revenge\|revenge]] is now at Milford. Would I had wings to follow it. Come, and be true. Exit |
| PISANIO | Thou bidd’st me to my loss, for true to thee<br>Were to prove false, which I will never be<br>To him that is most true. To Milford go,<br>And find not her whom thou pursuest. Flow, flow,<br>You heavenly blessings, on her. This [[archetypes/fool\|fool]]’s [[characters/speed\|speed]]<br>Be crossed with slowness; labour be his meed. Exit |

### Atto 3, Scena 6

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]], dressed as a man, before the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I see a man’s life is a tedious one.<br>I have tired myself, and for two nights together<br>Have made the ground my bed. I should be sick,<br>But that my resolution helps me. Milford,<br>When from the mountain-top Pisanio showed thee,<br>Thou wast within a ken. O Jove, I think<br>Foundations fly the wretched—such, I mean,<br>Where they should be relieved. Two beggars told me<br>I could not miss my way. Will poor folks lie,<br>That have afflictions on them, knowing ‘tis<br>A punishment or trial? Yes. No [[concepts/wonder\|wonder]],<br>When rich ones scarce tell true. To lapse in fullness<br>Is sorer than to lie for need, and falsehood<br>Is worse in kings than beggars. My dear lord,<br>Thou art one o’th’ false ones. Now I think on thee<br>My hunger’s gone, but even before I was<br>At point to sink for food. But what is this?<br>Here is a path to’t. ‘Tis some savage hold.<br>I were best not call; I dare not call; yet famine,<br>Ere clean it o’erthrow [[concepts/nature\|nature]], makes it valiant.<br>Plenty and peace breeds cowards, hardness ever<br>Of hardiness is mother. Ho! Who’s here?<br>If anything that’s civil, speak; if savage,<br>Take or lend. Ho! No answer? Then I’ll enter.<br>Best draw my sword, and if mine enemy<br>But [[concepts/fear\|fear]] the sword like me he’ll scarcely look on’t.<br>Such a foe, good heavens! |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit into the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]], and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | You, Polydore, have proved best woodman and<br>Are master of the feast. Cadwal and I<br>Will play the cook and servant; ‘tis our match.<br>The sweat of industry would dry and die<br>But for the end it works to. Come, our stomachs<br>Will make what’s homely savoury. Weariness<br>Can snore upon the flint when resty sloth<br>Finds the down pillow hard. Now peace be here,<br>Poor house, that keep’st thyself. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I am throughly weary. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | I am weak with toil yet strong in appetite. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | There is cold meat i’th’ [[motifs/cave\|cave]]. We’ll browse on that<br>Whilst what we have killed be cooked. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | (looking into the [[motifs/cave\|cave]]) Stay, come not in.<br>But that it eats our victuals I should think<br>Here were a fairy. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | What’s the matter, sir? |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | By Jupiter, an angel—or, if not,<br>An earthly paragon. Behold divineness<br>No elder than a boy. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]] from the [[motifs/cave\|cave]], dressed as a man |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Good masters, harm me not.<br>Before I entered here I called, and thought<br>To have begged or bought what I have took. Good<br>[[concepts/truth\|truth]],<br>I have stol’n naught, nor would not, though I had<br>found<br>Gold strewed i’th’ floor. Here’s money for my meat.<br>I would have left it on the board so soon<br>As I had made my meal, and parted<br>With prayers for the provider. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Money, youth? |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | All gold and silver rather turn to dirt,<br>As ’tis no better reckoned but of those<br>Who worship dirty gods. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I see you’re angry.<br>Know, if you kill me for my fault, I should<br>Have died had I not made it. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Whither bound? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | To Milford Haven. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | What’s your name? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Fidele, sir. I have a kinsman who<br>Is bound for [[settings/italy\|Italy]]. He embarked at Milford,<br>To whom being going, almost spent with hunger,<br>I am fall’n in this offence. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Prithee, fair youth,<br>Think us no churls, nor measure our good minds<br>By this rude place we live in. [[motifs/well\|Well]] encountered.<br>’Tis almost [[motifs/night\|night]]. You shall have better cheer<br>Ere you depart, and thanks to stay and eat it.<br>Boys, bid him welcome. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Were you a woman, youth,<br>I should woo hard but be your groom in honesty,<br>Ay, bid for you as I’d buy. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | I’ll make’t my comfort<br>He is a man, I’ll [[motifs/love\|love]] him as my brother.<br>(To [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) And such a welcome as I’d give to him<br>After long absence, such is yours. Most welcome.<br>Be sprightly, for you fall ’mongst friends. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | ’Mongst friends<br>If brothers. (Aside) Would it had been so that they<br>Had been my father’s sons. Then had my price<br>Been less, and so more equal ballasting<br>To thee, [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]].<br>The three men speak apart |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | He wrings at some distress. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Would I could free’t. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Or I, whate’er it be,<br>What [[motifs/pain\|pain]] it cost, what danger. Gods! |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Hark, boys.<br>They whisper |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | (aside) Great men<br>That had a [[settings/court\|court]] no bigger than this [[motifs/cave\|cave]],<br>That did attend themselves and had the virtue<br>Which their own [[concepts/conscience\|conscience]] sealed them, laying by<br>That nothing-gift of differing multitudes,<br>Could not outpeer these twain. Pardon me, gods,<br>I’d change my sex to be companion with them,<br>Since Leonatus’ false. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | It shall be so.<br>Boys, we’ll go dress our hunt. Fair youth, come in.<br>Discourse is heavy, fasting. When we have supped<br>We’ll mannerly demand thee of thy story,<br>So far as thou wilt speak it. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Pray draw near. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | The [[motifs/night\|night]] to th’ owl and morn to th’ lark less welcome. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Thanks, sir. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | I pray draw near. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt into the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] |

### Atto 3, Scena 7

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter two Roman Senators, and Tribunes |
| FIRST SENATOR | This is the tenor of the Emperor’s writ:<br>That since the common men are now in action<br>‘Gainst the Pannonians and Dalmatians,<br>And that the legions now in Gallia are<br>Full weak to undertake our wars against<br>The fall’n-off Britons, that we do incite<br>The gentry to this business. He creates<br>[[characters/lucius\|Lucius]] pro-consul, and to you the tribunes,<br>For this immediate levy, he commends<br>His absolute commission. Long live Caesar!<br>A TRIBUNE<br>Is [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]] general of the forces? |
| SECOND SENATOR | Ay.<br>A TRIBUNE<br>Remaining now in Gallia? |
| FIRST SENATOR | With those legions<br>Which I have spoke of, whereunto your levy<br>Must be supplyant. The words of your commission<br>Will tie you to the numbers and the [[motifs/time\|time]]<br>Of their dispatch.<br>A TRIBUNE<br>We will discharge our duty. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt |

### Atto 4, Scena 1

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], in [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]’ suit |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | I am near to th’ place where they should meet, if Pisanio have mapped it truly. How fit his garments serve me! Why should his mistress, who was made by him that made the tailor, not be fit too?—the rather—saving reverence of the word—for ’tis said a woman’s fitness comes by fits. Therein I must play the workman. I dare speak it to myself, for it is not vainglory for a man and his glass to confer in his own chamber. I mean the lines of my [[concepts/body\|body]] are as [[motifs/well\|well]] drawn as his: no less young, more strong, not beneath him in fortunes, beyond him in the advantage of the [[motifs/time\|time]], above him in birth, alike conversant in general services, and more remarkable in single oppositions. Yet this imperceiverant thing loves him in my despite. What [[concepts/mortality\|mortality]] is! [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]], thy head which now is growing upon thy shoulders shall within this hour be off, thy mistress enforced, thy garments cut to pieces before thy face; and all this done, spurn her [[motifs/home\|home]] to her father, who may haply be a little angry for my so rough usage; but my mother, having power of his testiness, shall turn all into my commendations. My [[motifs/horse\|horse]] is tied up safe. Out, sword, and to a sore purpose! Fortune, put them into my hand. This is the very description of their meeting-place, and the fellow dares not deceive me. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit |

### Atto 4, Scena 2

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]], [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]], and [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]] dressed as a man, from the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]])<br>You are not [[motifs/well\|well]]. Remain here in the [[motifs/cave\|cave]].<br>We’ll come to you from hunting. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]])<br>Brother, stay here.<br>Are we not brothers? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | So man and man should be,<br>But clay and clay differs in dignity,<br>Whose [[motifs/dust\|dust]] is both alike. I am very sick. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | (to [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]] and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]])<br>Go you to hunting. I’ll abide with him. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | So sick I am not, yet I am not [[motifs/well\|well]];<br>But not so citizen a wanton as<br>To seem to die ere sick. So please you, leave me.<br>Stick to your journal course. The breach of custom<br>Is breach of all. I am ill, but your being by me<br>Cannot amend me. Society is no comfort<br>To one not sociable. I am not very sick,<br>Since I can reason of it. Pray you, trust me here.<br>I’ll rob none but myself; and let me die,<br>Stealing so poorly. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I [[motifs/love\|love]] thee: I have spoke it;<br>How much the quantity, the weight as much,<br>As I do [[motifs/love\|love]] my father. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | What, how, how? |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | If it be sin to say so, sir, I yoke me<br>In my good brother’s fault. I know not why<br>I [[motifs/love\|love]] this youth, and I have heard you say<br>[[motifs/love\|Love]]’s reason’s without reason. The bier at door<br>And a demand who is’t shall die, I’d say<br>‘My father, not this youth’. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | (aside)<br>O noble strain!<br>O worthiness of [[concepts/nature\|nature]], breed of [[concepts/greatness\|greatness]]!<br>Cowards father cowards, and base things sire base.<br>[[concepts/nature\|Nature]] hath meal and bran, contempt and grace.<br>I’m not their father, yet who this should be<br>Doth miracle itself, loved before me.<br>(Aloud) ‘Tis the ninth hour o’th’ morn. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]])<br>Brother, farewell. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I wish ye sport. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | You health.—So please you, sir. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | (aside)<br>These are kind creatures. Gods, what lies I have heard!<br>Our courtiers say all’s savage but at [[settings/court\|court]].<br>Experience, O thou disprov‘st report!<br>Th’imperious seas breeds monsters; for the dish<br>Poor tributary rivers as sweet fish.<br>I am sick still, heart-sick. Pisanio,<br>I’ll now taste of thy drug. |
| *(didascalia)* | She swallows the drug. The men speak apart |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I could not stir him.<br>He said he was gentle but unfortunate,<br>Dishonestly afflicted but yet honest. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Thus did he answer me, yet said hereafter<br>I might know more. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | To th’ field, to th’ field!<br>(To [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) We’ll leave you for this [[motifs/time\|time]]. Go in and rest. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]])<br>We’ll not be long away. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]])<br>Pray be not sick,<br>For you must be our housewife. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | [[motifs/well\|Well]] or ill,<br>I am bound to you. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | And shalt be ever.<br>This youth, howe’er distressed, appears hath had<br>Good ancestors. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | How angel-like he sings! |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | But his neat cookery! |
| *(didascalia)* | [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | He cut our roots in characters,<br>And sauced our broths as Juno had been sick<br>And he her dieter. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Nobly he yokes<br>A smiling with a sigh, as if the sigh<br>Was that it was for not being such a smile;<br>The smile mocking the sigh that it would fly<br>From so divine a temple to commix<br>With winds that sailors rail at. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I do note<br>That grief and patience, rooted in him both,<br>Mingle their spurs together. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Grow patience,<br>And let the stinking elder, grief, untwine<br>His perishing root with the increasing vine. |
| RELARIUS | It is great morning. Come away. Who’s there? |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] in [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]’ suit |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | I cannot find those runagates. That [[archetypes/villain\|villain]]<br>Hath mocked me. I am faint. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | (aside to [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] and [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]])<br>‘Those runagates’?<br>Means he not us? I partly know him; ‘tis<br>[[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], the son o’th’ [[characters/queen\|Queen]]. I [[concepts/fear\|fear]] some ambush.<br>I saw him not these many years, and yet<br>I know ’tis he. We are held as outlaws. Hence! |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | (aside to [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] and [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]])<br>He is but one. You and my brother search<br>What companies are near. Pray you, away.<br>Let me alone with him. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] and [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]] |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Soft, what are you<br>That fly me thus? Some [[archetypes/villain\|villain]] mountaineers?<br>I have heard of such. What slave art thou? |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | A thing<br>More slavish did I ne’er than answering<br>A slave without a knock. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Thou art a robber,<br>A law-breaker, a [[archetypes/villain\|villain]]. Yield thee, thief. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | To who? To thee? What art thou? Have not I<br>An arm as big as thine, a heart as big?<br>Thy words, I grant, are bigger, for I wear not<br>My dagger in my mouth. Say what thou art,<br>Why I should yield to thee. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Thou [[archetypes/villain\|villain]] base,<br>Know’st me not by my clothes? |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | No, nor thy tailor, rascal,<br>Who is thy grandfather. He made those clothes,<br>Which, as it seems, make thee. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Thou precious varlet,<br>My tailor made them not. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Hence, then, and thank<br>The man that gave them thee. Thou art some [[archetypes/fool\|fool]].<br>I am loath to beat thee. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Thou injurious thief,<br>Hear but my name and tremble.<br>GUlDERIUS<br>What’s thy name? |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], thou [[archetypes/villain\|villain]]. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], thou [[topoi/double\|double]] [[archetypes/villain\|villain]], be thy name,<br>I cannot tremble at it. Were it toad or adder, spider,<br>’Twould move me sooner. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | To thy further [[concepts/fear\|fear]],<br>Nay, to thy mere confusion, thou shalt know<br>I am son to th’ [[characters/queen\|Queen]]. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I am sorry for’t, not seeming<br>So worthy as thy birth. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Art not afeard? |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Those that I reverence, those I [[concepts/fear\|fear]], the wise.<br>At fools I laugh, not [[concepts/fear\|fear]] them. |
| [[characters/cloten\|CLOTEN]] | Die the [[motifs/death\|death]].<br>When I have slain thee with my proper hand<br>I’ll follow those that even now fled hence,<br>And on the gates of Lud’s town set your heads.<br>Yield, rustic mountaineer.<br>Fight and exeunt |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]] and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | No company’s abroad? |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | None in the world. You did mistake him, sure. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | I cannot tell. Long is it since I saw him,<br>But [[motifs/time\|time]] hath nothing blurred those lines of favour<br>Which then he wore. The snatches in his voice<br>And burst of speaking were as his. I am absolute<br>’Twas very [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | In this place we left them.<br>I wish my brother make good [[motifs/time\|time]] with him,<br>You say he is so fell. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Being scarce made up,<br>I mean to man, he had not apprehension<br>Of roaring terrors; for defect of judgement<br>Is oft the cause of [[concepts/fear\|fear]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]] with [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s head |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | But see, thy brother. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | This [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] was a [[archetypes/fool\|fool]], an empty purse,<br>There was no money in’t. Not Hercules<br>Could have knocked out his brains, for he had none.<br>Yet I not doing this, the [[archetypes/fool\|fool]] had borne<br>My head as I do his. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | What hast thou done? |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | I am perfect what: cut off one [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s head,<br>Son to the [[characters/queen\|Queen]] after his own report,<br>Who called me traitor, mountaineer, and swore<br>With his own single hand he’d take us in,<br>Displace our heads where—thanks, ye gods—they<br>grow,<br>And set them on Lud’s town. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | We are all undone. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Why, worthy father, what have we to lose<br>But that he swore to take, our lives? The law<br>Protects not us: then why should we be tender<br>To let an arrogant piece of flesh threat us,<br>Play judge and executioner all himself,<br>For we do [[concepts/fear\|fear]] the law? What company<br>Discover you abroad? |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | No single [[motifs/soul\|soul]]<br>Can we set eye on, but in all safe reason<br>He must have some attendants. Though his humour<br>Was nothing but mutation, ay, and that<br>From one bad thing to worse, not frenzy,<br>Not absolute [[concepts/madness\|madness]], could so far have raved<br>To bring him here alone. Although perhaps<br>It may be heard at [[settings/court\|court]] that such as we<br>[[motifs/cave\|Cave]] here, hunt here, are outlaws, and in [[motifs/time\|time]]<br>May make some stronger head, the which he<br>hearing—<br>As it is like him—might break out, and swear<br>He’d fetch us in, yet is’t not probable<br>To come alone, either he so undertaking,<br>Or they so [[concepts/suffering\|suffering]]. Then on good ground we [[concepts/fear\|fear]]<br>If we do [[concepts/fear\|fear]] this [[concepts/body\|body]] hath a tail<br>More perilous than the head. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Let ord’nance<br>Come as the gods foresay it; howsoe’er,<br>My brother hath done [[motifs/well\|well]]. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | I had no mind<br>To hunt this day. The boy Fidele’s sickness<br>Did make my way long forth.<br>GUIDERlUS<br>With his own sword,<br>Which he did wave against my throat, I have ta’en<br>His head from him. I’ll throw’t into the creek<br>Behind our rock, and let it to the sea<br>And tell the fishes he’s the [[characters/queen\|Queen]]’s son, [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]].<br>That’s all I reck. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit with [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s head |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | I [[concepts/fear\|fear]] ’twill be revenged.<br>Would, Polydore, thou hadst not done’t, though<br>valour<br>Becomes thee [[motifs/well\|well]] enough. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Would I had done’t,<br>So the [[concepts/revenge\|revenge]] alone pursued me. Polydore,<br>I [[motifs/love\|love]] thee brotherly, but envy much<br>Thou hast robbed me of this deed. I would revenges<br>That possible strength might meet would seek us<br>through<br>And put us to our answer. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | [[motifs/well\|Well]], ’tis done.<br>We’ll hunt no more today, nor seek for danger<br>Where there’s no profit. I prithee, to our rock.<br>You and Fidele play the cooks. I’ll stay<br>Till hasty Polydore return, and bring him<br>To dinner presently. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Poor sick Fidele!<br>I’ll willingly to him. To gain his colour<br>I’d let a parish of such Clotens [[motifs/blood\|blood]],<br>And praise myself for [[concepts/charity\|charity]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit into the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | O thou goddess,<br>Thou divine [[concepts/nature\|Nature]], how thyself thou blazon‘st<br>In these two princely boys! They are as gentle<br>As zephyrs blowing below the violet,<br>Not wagging his sweet head; and yet as rough,<br>Their royal [[motifs/blood\|blood]] enchafed, as the rud’st [[motifs/wind\|wind]]<br>That by the top doth take the mountain pine<br>And make him stoop to th’ vale. ’Tis [[concepts/wonder\|wonder]]<br>That an invisible instinct should frame them<br>To royalty unlearned, [[concepts/honour\|honour]] untaught,<br>Civility not seen from other, valour<br>That wildly grows in them, but yields a crop<br>As if it had been sowed. Yet still it’s strange<br>What [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s being here to us portends,<br>Or what his [[motifs/death\|death]] will bring us. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]] |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Where’s my brother?<br>I have sent [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s clotpoll down the stream<br>In embassy to his mother. His [[concepts/body\|body]]’s hostage<br>For his return.<br>Solemn music |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | My ingenious instrument!—<br>Hark, Polydore, it sounds. But what occasion<br>Hath Cadwal now to give it motion? Hark! |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Is he at [[motifs/home\|home]]? |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | He went hence even now. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | What does he mean? Since [[motifs/death\|death]] of my dear’st mother<br>It did not speak before. All solemn things<br>Should answer solemn accidents. The matter?<br>Triumphs for nothing and lamenting toys<br>Is jollity for apes and grief for boys.<br>Is Cadwal mad? |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter from the [[motifs/cave\|cave]] [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] with [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]], dead, bearing her in his arms |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Look, here he comes,<br>And brings the dire occasion in his arms<br>Of what we blame him for. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | The bird is dead<br>That we have made so much on. I had rather<br>Have skipped from sixteen years of age to sixty,<br>To have turned my leaping [[motifs/time\|time]] into a crutch,<br>Than have seen this. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) O sweetest, fairest lily!<br>My brother wears thee not one half so [[motifs/well\|well]]<br>As when thou grew’st thyself. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | O [[concepts/melancholy\|melancholy]],<br>Who ever yet could sound thy [[characters/bottom\|bottom]], find<br>The ooze to show what coast thy sluggish crare<br>Might easiliest harbour in? Thou blessèd thing,<br>Jove knows what man thou mightst have made;<br>but I,<br>Thou diedst a most rare boy, of [[concepts/melancholy\|melancholy]].<br>(To [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]]) How found you him? |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Stark, as you see,<br>Thus smiling as some fly had tickled slumber,<br>Not as [[motifs/death\|death]]’s dart being laughed at; his right cheek<br>Reposing on a cushion. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Where? |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | O’th’ floor,<br>His arms thus leagued. I thought he slept, and put<br>My clouted brogues from off my feet, whose rudeness<br>Answered my steps too loud. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Why, he but sleeps.<br>If he be gone he’ll make his [[motifs/grave\|grave]] a bed.<br>With female fairies will his tomb be haunted,<br>(To [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) And worms will not come to thee. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]]) With fairest [[motifs/flowers\|flowers]]<br>Whilst [[motifs/summer\|summer]] lasts and I live here, Fidele,<br>I’ll sweeten thy sad [[motifs/grave\|grave]]. Thou shalt not lack<br>The flower that’s like thy face, pale primrose, nor<br>The azured harebell, like thy veins; no, nor<br>The leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander<br>Outsweetened not thy breath. The ruddock would<br>With charitable bill—O bill sore shaming<br>Those rich-left heirs that let their fathers lie<br>Without a monument!—bring thee all this,<br>Yea, and furred moss besides, when [[motifs/flowers\|flowers]] are none,<br>To [[motifs/winter\|winter]]-gown thy corpse. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Prithee, have done,<br>And do not play in wench-like words with that<br>Which is so serious. Let us bury him,<br>And not protract with admiration what<br>Is now due debt. To th’ [[motifs/grave\|grave]]. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Say, where shall ’s lay him? |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | By good Euriphile, our mother. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Be’t SO,<br>And let us, Polydore, though now our voices<br>Have got the mannish crack, sing him to th’ ground<br>As once our mother; use like note and words,<br>Save that ‘Euriphile’ must be ‘Fidele’. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Cadwal,<br>I cannot sing. I’ll weep, and word it with thee,<br>For notes of sorrow out of tune are worse<br>Than priests and fanes that lie. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | We’ll speak it then. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Great griefs, I see, medicine the less, for [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]<br>Is quite forgot. He was a [[characters/queen\|queen]]’s son, boys,<br>And though he came our enemy, remember<br>He was paid for that. Though mean and mighty<br>rotting<br>Together have one [[motifs/dust\|dust]], yet reverence,<br>That angel of the world, doth make distinction<br>Of place ’tween high and low. Our foe was princely,<br>And though you took his life as being our foe,<br>Yet bury him as a prince. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Pray you, fetch him hither.<br>[[characters/thersites\|Thersites]]’ [[concepts/body\|body]] is as good as [[characters/ajax\|Ajax]]’<br>When neither are alive. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | (to [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]]) If you’ll go fetch him,<br>We’ll say our song the whilst. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]] |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Brother, begin. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Nay, Cadwal, we must lay his head to th’east.<br>My father hath a reason for’t. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | ’Tis true. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | Come on, then, and remove him. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | So, begin. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | [[concepts/fear\|Fear]] no more the heat o‘th’ sun,<br>Nor the furious [[motifs/winter\|winter]]’s rages.<br>Thou thy worldly task hast done,<br>[[motifs/home\|Home]] art gone and ta’en thy wages.<br>Golden lads and girls all must,<br>As chimney-sweepers, come to [[motifs/dust\|dust]]. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | [[concepts/fear\|Fear]] no more the frown o’th’ great,<br>Thou art past the [[archetypes/tyrant\|tyrant]]’s stroke.<br>Care no more to clothe and eat,<br>To thee the reed is as the oak.<br>The sceptre, learning, physic, must<br>All follow this and come to [[motifs/dust\|dust]]. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | [[concepts/fear\|Fear]] no more the [[motifs/lightning\|lightning]] flash, |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Nor th’all-dreaded thunder-stone. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | [[concepts/fear\|Fear]] not slander, censure rash. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Thou hast finished joy and moan. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | and [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]]<br>All lovers young, all lovers must<br>Consign to thee and come to [[motifs/dust\|dust]]. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | No exorcisor harm thee, |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Nor no witchcraft charm thee. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | [[archetypes/ghost\|Ghost]] unlaid forbear thee. |
| [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]] | Nothing ill come near thee. |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | and [[characters/arviragus\|ARVIRAGUS]]<br>Quiet consummation have,<br>And renowned be thy [[motifs/grave\|grave]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]] with the [[concepts/body\|body]] of [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]] in [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]’ suit |
| [[characters/guiderius\|GUIDERIUS]] | We have done our obsequies. Come, lay him down. |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | Here’s a few [[motifs/flowers\|flowers]], but ‘bout midnight more;<br>The herbs that have on them cold dew o’th’ [[motifs/night\|night]]<br>Are strewings fitt‘st for graves upon th’earth’s face.<br>You were as [[motifs/flowers\|flowers]], now withered; even so<br>These herblets shall, which we upon you strow.<br>Come on, away; apart upon our knees |
| *(didascalia)* |  |
| [[characters/belarius\|BELARIUS]] | The ground that gave them first has them again.<br>Their pleasures here are past, so is their [[motifs/pain\|pain]]. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]], and [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]] |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | (awakes)<br>Yes, sir, to Milford Haven. Which is the way?<br>I thank you. By yon bush? Pray, how far thither?<br>‘Od’s pitykins, can it be six mile yet?<br>I have gone all [[motifs/night\|night]]. ’[[concepts/faith\|Faith]], I’ll lie down and [[motifs/sleep\|sleep]].<br>She sees [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]<br>But soft, no bedfellow! O gods and goddesses!<br>These [[motifs/flowers\|flowers]] are like the pleasures of the world,<br>This bloody man the care on’t. I [[concepts/hope\|hope]] I dream,<br>For so I thought I was a cavekeeper,<br>And cook to honest creatures. But ‘tis not so.<br>’Twas but a bolt of nothing, shot of nothing,<br>Which the brain makes of fumes. Our very eyes<br>Are sometimes like our judgements, blind. Good [[concepts/faith\|faith]],<br>I tremble still with [[concepts/fear\|fear]]; but if there be<br>Yet left in heaven as small a drop of pity<br>As a wren’s eye, feared gods, a part of it!<br>The dream’s here still. Even when I wake it is<br>Without me as within me; not imagined, felt.<br>A headless man? The garments of [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]]?<br>I know the shape of ’s leg; this is his hand,<br>His foot Mercurial, his Martial thigh,<br>The brawns of Hercules; but his Jovial face-<br>Murder in heaven! How? ‘Tis gone. Pisanio,<br>All curses madded Hecuba gave the Greeks,<br>And mine to boot, be darted on thee! Thou,<br>Conspired with that irregulous devil [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]],<br>Hath here cut off my lord. To write and read<br>Be henceforth treacherous! Damned Pisanio<br>Hath with his forged letters-damned Pisanio-<br>From this most bravest vessel of the world<br>Struck the main-top) O [[characters/posthumus\|Posthumus]], alas,<br>Where is thy head? Where’s that? Ay me, where’s<br>that?<br>Pisanio might have killed thee at the heart<br>And left thy head on. How should this be? Pisanio?<br>’Tis he and [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]. Malice and lucre in them<br>Have laid this woe here. O, ‘tis pregnant, pregnant!<br>The drug he gave me, which he said was precious<br>And cordial to me, have I not found it<br>Murd’rous to th’ senses? That confirms it [[motifs/home\|home]].<br>This is Pisanio’s deed, and [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]-O,<br>Give colour to my pale cheek with thy [[motifs/blood\|blood]],<br>That we the horrider may seem to those<br>Which chance to find usl |
| *(didascalia)* | She smears her face with [[motifs/blood\|blood]] |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | O my lord, my lord! |
| *(didascalia)* | She faints. |
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]], Roman Captains, and a Soothsayer |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | A ROMAN CAPTAIN (to [[characters/lucius\|Lucius]])<br>To them the legions garrisoned in Gallia<br>After your will have crossed the sea, attending<br>You here at Milford Haven with your ships.<br>They are hence in readiness. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | But what from Rome?<br>A ROMAN CAPTAIN<br>The senate hath stirred up the confiners<br>And gentlemen of [[settings/italy\|Italy]], most willing spirits<br>That promise noble service, and they come<br>Under the conduct of bold Giacomo,<br>Siena’s brother. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | When expect you them?<br>A ROMAN CAPTAIN<br>With the next benefit o’th’ [[motifs/wind\|wind]]. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | This forwardness<br>Makes our hopes fair. Command our present numbers<br>Be mustered; bid the captains look to’t. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit one or more |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | (To Soothsayer) Now, sir,<br>What have you dreamed of late of this war’s purpose? |
| SOOTHSAYER | Last [[motifs/night\|night]] the very gods showed me a vision—<br>I fast, and prayed for their intelligence-thus:<br>I saw Jove’s bird, the Roman eagle, winged<br>From the spongy south to this part of the west,<br>There vanished in the sunbeams; which portends,<br>Unless my sins abuse my divination,<br>Success to th’ Roman host. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Dream often so,<br>And never false.<br>He sees [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s [[concepts/body\|body]]<br>Soft, ho, what trunk is here<br>Without his top? The ruin speaks that sometime<br>It was a worthy building. How, a page?<br>Or dead or sleeping on him? But dead rather,<br>For [[concepts/nature\|nature]] doth abhor to make his bed<br>With the defunct, or [[motifs/sleep\|sleep]] upon the dead.<br>Let’s see the boy’s face.<br>A ROMAN CAPTAIN<br>He’s alive, my lord. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | He’ll then instruct us of this [[concepts/body\|body]]. Young one,<br>Inform us of thy fortunes, for it seems<br>They crave to be demanded. Who is this<br>Thou mak’st thy bloody pillow? Or who was he<br>That, otherwise than noble [[concepts/nature\|nature]] did,<br>Hath altered that good picture? What’s thy interest<br>In this sad wreck? How came’t? Who is’t?<br>What art thou? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I am nothing; or if not,<br>Nothing to be were better. This was my master,<br>A very valiant Briton, and a good,<br>That here by mountaineers lies slain. Alas,<br>There is no more such masters. I may wander<br>From east to occident, cry out for service,<br>Try many, all good; serve truly, never<br>Find such another master. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | ’Lack, good youth,<br>Thou mov’st no less with thy complaining than<br>Thy master in bleeding. Say his name, good friend. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | [[characters/richard\|Richard]] du Champ. (Aside) If I do lie and do<br>No harm by it, though the gods hear I [[concepts/hope\|hope]]<br>They’ll pardon it. (Aloud) Say you, sir? |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Thy name? |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | Fidele, sir. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Thou dost approve thyself the very same.<br>Thy name [[motifs/well\|well]] fits thy [[concepts/faith\|faith]], thy [[concepts/faith\|faith]] thy name.<br>Wilt take thy chance with me? I will not say<br>Thou shalt be so [[motifs/well\|well]] mastered, but be sure,<br>No less beloved. The Roman Emperor’s letters<br>Sent by a consul to me should not sooner<br>Than thine own worth prefer thee. Go with me. |
| [[characters/innogen\|INNOGEN]] | I’ll follow, sir. But first, an’t please the gods,<br>I’ll hide my master from the flies as deep<br>As these poor pickaxes can dig; and when<br>With wild-wood [[motifs/leaves\|leaves]] and weeds I ha’ strewed his<br>[[motifs/grave\|grave]]<br>And on it said a century of prayers,<br>Such as I can, twice o’er I’ll weep and sigh,<br>And leaving so his service, follow you,<br>So please you entertain me. |
| [[characters/lucius\|LUCIUS]] | Ay, good youth,<br>And rather father thee than master thee. My friends,<br>The boy hath taught us manly duties. Let us<br>Find out the prettiest daisied plot we can,<br>And make him with our pikes and partisans<br>A [[motifs/grave\|grave]]. Come, arm him. Boy, he is preferred<br>By thee to us, and he shall be interred<br>As soldiers can. Be cheerful. Wipe thine eyes.<br>Some falls are means the happier to arise. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt with [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]]’s [[concepts/body\|body]] |

### Atto 4, Scena 3

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]], Lords, and Pisanio |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Again, and bring me word how ’tis with her. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit one or more |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | A fever with the absence of her son,<br>A [[concepts/madness\|madness]] of which her life’s in danger-heavens,<br>How deeply you at once do touch me! [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]],<br>The great part of my comfort, gone; my [[characters/queen\|queen]]<br>Upon a desperate bed, and in a [[motifs/time\|time]]<br>When fearful wars point at me; her son gone,<br>So needful for this present! It strikes me past<br>The [[concepts/hope\|hope]] of comfort. (To Pisanio) But for thee, fellow,<br>Who needs must know of her departure and<br>Dost seem so ignorant, we’ll enforce it from thee<br>By a sharp torture. |
| PISANIO | Sir, my life is yours.<br>I humbly set it at your will. But for my mistress,<br>I nothing know where she remains, why gone,<br>Nor when she purposes return. Beseech your<br>highness,<br>Hold me your loyal servant.<br>A LORD<br>Good my liege,<br>The day that she was missing he was here.<br>I dare be bound he’s true, and shall perform<br>All parts of his subjection loyally. For [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]],<br>There wants no diligence in seeking him,<br>And will no [[concepts/doubt\|doubt]] be found. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | The [[motifs/time\|time]] is troublesome.<br>(To Pisanio) We’ll slip you for a season, but our [[concepts/jealousy\|jealousy]]<br>Does yet depend.<br>A LORD<br>So please your majesty,<br>The Roman legions, all from Gallia drawn,<br>Are landed on your coast with a supply<br>Of Roman gentlemen by the senate sent. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | Now for the counsel of my son and [[characters/queen\|queen]]!<br>I am amazed with matter.<br>A LORD<br>Good my liege,<br>Your preparation can affront no less<br>Than what you hear of. Come more, for more you’re<br>ready.<br>The want is but to put those powers in motion<br>That long to move. |
| [[characters/cymbeline\|CYMBELINE]] | I thank you. Let’s withdraw,<br>And meet the [[motifs/time\|time]] as it seeks us. We [[concepts/fear\|fear]] not<br>What can from [[settings/italy\|Italy]] annoy us, but<br>We grieve at chances here. Away. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exeunt [[characters/cymbeline\|Cymbeline]] and Lords |
| PISANIO | I heard no letter from my master since<br>I wrote him [[characters/innogen\|Innogen]] was slain. ‘Tis strange.<br>Nor hear I from my mistress, who did promise<br>To yield me often tidings. Neither know I<br>What is betid to [[characters/cloten\|Cloten]], but remain<br>Perplexed in all. The heavens still must work.<br>Wherein I am false I am honest; not true, to be true.<br>These present wars shall find I [[motifs/love\|love]] my country<br>Even to the note o’th’ [[archetypes/king\|King]], or I’ll fall in them.<br>All other doubts, by [[motifs/time\|time]] let them be cleared:<br>Fortune brings in some boats that are not steered. |
| *(didascalia)* | Exit |

### Atto 4, Scena 4

| Speaker | Line |
|---|---|
| *(didascalia)* | Enter [[characters/belarius\|Belarius]], [[characters/guiderius\|Guiderius]], and [[characters/arviragus\|Arviragus]] |
